First, we write the integral as

$$
\int 2\operatorname{ln}⁡4x\,\text{d}x=2\int \operatorname{ln}⁡4x\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & =2\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =2[\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =2[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-\int \,\text{d}x] \\  & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-2x+C \\  & =2x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.
